title: Netlify configuration
description: Configuration for a Netlify project, set in the `netlify.toml` file, which specifies how Netlify builds and deploys your site. See https://docs.netlify.com/build/configure-builds/file-based-configuration/.

$schema.description: URL of the JSON schema that describes this file, which editors use to validate it and suggest properties. Netlify does not use it.

context.description: Settings that apply to a kind of deploy. Any property in `[context.production]`, `[context.deploy-preview]`, `[context.branch-deploy]`, or `[context.dev]` will override less specific contexts, and any property in `[context.branchname]`, for a given branchname, is the most specific. A branch name that ends in `*` matches branches by prefix. See https://docs.netlify.com/build/configure-builds/file-based-configuration/#deploy-contexts.

dev.description: Optional configuration for Netlify Dev, the local development environment. Note that `[dev]` doesn't run in the Bash shell, so you won't be able to use Bash-compatible syntax with the command. To set environment variables for local development, use `[context.dev.environment]` instead. See https://docs.netlify.com/build/configure-builds/file-based-configuration/#netlify-dev.

headers.description: Custom headers. By default, headers set in the `netlify.toml` are global for all builds and cannot be scoped for specific branches or deploy contexts. See https://docs.netlify.com/manage/routing/headers/.

images.description: Settings for Netlify Image CDN. See https://docs.netlify.com/build/image-cdn/overview/.

remote_images.description: Allowed domains for remote source images, as an array of regex. In the regex, escape literal dots (`\.`); forward slashes don't need escaping.

redirects.description: Redirect and rewrite rules. Redirects are global for all builds and do not get scoped to deploy contexts. See https://docs.netlify.com/manage/routing/redirects/overview/#syntax-for-the-netlify-configuration-file.

spa_fallback.description: Whether to add a catch-all rule that rewrites every path to `/index.html` with a `200` status, for single-page apps that handle routing internally. It is not added if a rule for `/*` already exists.

build.description: Build settings. Settings for the `[build]` key are global and are applied to all deploy contexts unless overridden by a context-specific setting.

base.description: Directory where Netlify checks for dependency management files such as `package.json` or `.nvmrc`, installs dependencies, and runs your build command. If not set, the base directory defaults to the root of the repository.

command.description: The command to run to build your site if you are using a static site generator or other build tool. For example, `npm run build`. The build command runs in the Bash shell, allowing you to add Bash-compatible syntax to the command.

edge_functions.description: Custom edge functions directory, as an absolute path relative to the site's base directory. The default edge functions directory is `YOUR_BASE_DIRECTORY/netlify/edge-functions`.

environment.description: Build environment variables. We recommend that you use the Netlify UI instead, to avoid storing sensitive values in your repository.

functions.description: Directory that contains function files and optional subdirectories for organizing function files. The functions directory is relative to the base directory. `functions.directory` takes precedence over this setting.

ignore.description: A Node.js or Bash command that runs from the base directory and determines whether or not the site needs rebuilding. An exit code of `1` indicates the contents have changed and the build process continues as usual. An exit code of `0` indicates that there are no changes and the build should stop.

publish.description: Directory that contains the deploy-ready HTML files and assets generated by the build. The directory is relative to the base directory, which is root by default (`/`).

contextConfig.description: Settings for this deploy context or branch. Build settings can be set directly, as in `[context.production]`, or under `build`.

edge_functions.description: A string sets the edge functions directory for this context, as `build.edge_functions` does. An array of tables declares edge functions for this context, as `[[edge_functions]]` does.

functions.description: A string sets the functions directory for this context, as `build.functions` does. A table sets functions settings for this context, as `[functions]` does.

path.description: Directory with the migrations that Netlify applies automatically. Defaults to `netlify/database/migrations`.

migrations.description: Settings for Netlify Database's native migration system.

edgeFunctions.description: Edge function declarations. Declaring edge functions in `netlify.toml` instead of inline in the function file lets you run multiple edge functions on the same path and customize the order they run in. See https://docs.netlify.com/build/edge-functions/declarations/#declare-edge-functions-in-netlifytoml.

cache.description: Optional setting to opt in to response caching, by setting it to `manual`.

excludedPath.description: Optional `URLPattern` exclusion to limit the routes matched by `path`. Accepts a single string or an array of strings.

excludedPattern.description: Optional regex exclusion to limit the routes matched by `pattern`. Accepts a single regex or an array of regex.

function.description: Name of the edge function you're configuring.

header.description: Optional conditions on HTTP headers that must be met for the edge function to run. Each key is the name of an HTTP header, and the value is `true` to match only if the header is present in the request, `false` to match only if it is not present, or a string to match only if the header value matches the regular expression represented in the string.

method.description: Optional HTTP methods that should run the edge function. Accepts a string or an array of strings.

name.description: Human-friendly name of the edge function.

path.description: `URLPattern` expression on which paths to run the edge function. Must start with `/`, for example `path = "/*"`.

pattern.description: Alternative to the `path` property that allows for regex path matching.

deno_import_map.description: Path to an import map file for edge functions, which maps module URLs to names so you can use module names in your import statements.

external_node_modules.description: List of Node.js modules that are copied to the bundled artifact without adjusting their source or references during the bundling process; only applies when `node_bundler` is set to `esbuild`. This property helps handle dependencies that can't be inlined, such as modules with native add-ons.

ignored_node_modules.description: List of Node.js modules to leave out of the function bundle.

included_files.description: List of additional paths to include in the function bundle. Although our build system includes statically referenced files (like `require("./some-file.js")`) by default, `included_files` lets you specify additional files or directories and reference them dynamically in function code. You can use `*` to match any character or prefix an entry with `!` to exclude files. Paths are absolute paths relative to the base directory.

memory.description: Memory for the function, as a number of megabytes or a human-friendly string with a unit (`"2gb"`, `"1024mb"`, case-insensitive). Allowed range: 1024 to 4096 MB. Memory and vCPU scale together, and the two are mutually exclusive; set one, not both.

node_bundler.description: Function bundling method used in @netlify/zip-it-and-ship-it. `esbuild` leverages esbuild to bundle functions, resulting in shorter bundling times and smaller artifacts, and TypeScript functions always use it. `zisi` is the default function bundling method for JavaScript functions.

region.description: Region the function runs in, identified by airport code, such as `dub`. The function-level region takes precedence over the site-level region set in the UI.

schedule.description: Cron expression for a scheduled function, in the format used by tools like crontab, executed according to the UTC timezone. For example, `0 0 * * *` runs every day at midnight UTC, and can also be written as `@daily`. The `@reboot` and `@annually` extensions are not supported.

vcpu.description: vCPUs for the function, as a number between 0.5 and 2.0. Memory and vCPU scale together, and the two are mutually exclusive; set one, not both.

functions.description: Optional, custom configuration for Netlify Functions. Settings at the top of `[functions]` apply to all functions in your project, and you can filter them by function name, including using glob patterns, as in `[functions."api_*"]`. If a function matches several configuration blocks containing one of these properties, the values are concatenated. See https://docs.netlify.com/build/configure-builds/file-based-configuration/#functions.

directory.description: Custom absolute path to your functions. The default location is `YOUR_BASE_DIRECTORY/netlify/functions`.

for.description: The path or URL where the headers will be added. Paths can contain wildcards (`*`), which match any character, and placeholders (`:placeholder`), which can only be used at the start of a path segment and match any character except `/`.

values.description: A map of values to add to the response headers. Multi-value headers are expressed with multi-line strings.

plugins.description: Build plugins, which extend the functionality of the build process. See https://docs.netlify.com/extend/install-and-use/build-plugins/#file-based-installation.

inputs.description: Custom settings that the plugin author may specify as required or available for configuring the plugin.

package.description: For a plugin installed from npm, the npm package name of the plugin. For a local plugin, the absolute path to a directory containing the plugin's `index.js` and `manifest.yml` files. The `package` value for a local plugin must start with `.` or `/`.

pinned_version.description: Major version of the plugin to use, such as `"1"`. When not set, Netlify pins the major version automatically.

conditions.description: Conditions to match the redirect, including country, role, and cookie presence conditions.

Country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to match, based on GeoIP data.

Language.description: Standard browser language identification codes, and locale codes that combine language and country, to match against the browser's language configuration.

Role.description: Roles to match, as authorized by Netlify Identity or any authentication provider that supports JSON Web Tokens (JWT).

force.description: Whether to override any existing content in the path or not; `false` by default.

from.description: The case-sensitive path you want to redirect. Special characters must be url-encoded.

headers.description: Additional request headers to send in proxy redirects.

query.description: Query string parameters required to match the redirect, each mapped to a placeholder such as `:path`.

rate_limit.description: Rate limit for requests that match the redirect, set with `window_limit`, `window_size` (in seconds, at most 180) and `aggregate_by` (`ip`, `domain` or both). See https://docs.netlify.com/manage/security/secure-access-to-sites/rate-limiting/#set-limits-for-redirects.

signed.description: Name of an environment variable for signed proxy redirects.

status.description: The HTTP status code you want to use in that redirect; `301` by default.

to.description: The URL or path you want to redirect to. Special characters must be url-encoded.

server.description: Settings for your project's Netlify Server. If your entry file also sets a property, the entry file takes precedence.

excludedPath.description: One or more URL paths that the server doesn't handle, using the same syntax as `path`. Requests for them go on to the rest of your project as if the server didn't exist.

includedFiles.description: Glob patterns for additional files to include in the server's bundle, such as data files your server reads at runtime. In `netlify.toml`, they're relative to your project's base directory. If the entry file also sets `includedFiles`, its patterns replace these.

path.description: One or more URL paths that the server handles. Paths must begin with a forward slash, and use the same syntax as function paths. Defaults to `/*`, which is every path that nothing else on your project handles.

region.description: Airport code of the region the server runs in: `cmh` for US East (Ohio) or `fra` for EU (Frankfurt). Defaults to `cmh`.

scale.description: How many instances your server runs. Netlify starts and stops instances as traffic changes, within these bounds.

max.description: The most instances that run at once. Defaults to the highest your plan allows.

min.description: The number of instances that keep running at all times, regardless of traffic. Defaults to `0`, so your server scales to zero when nothing is using it.

size.description: Size of the instances the server runs on: `small` (1 GB of memory, 1 shared vCPU), `medium` (2 GB, 1 vCPU) or `large` (4 GB, 2 vCPUs). Defaults to `small`.
